Main charitable entity types: Fundación (Código Civil, arts. 88-97); asociación (Código Civil); corporación (personas jurídicas de derecho privado) — registro ante Cámara de Comercio.

Main charitable entity types: Fundación (Ley Orgánica de Fundaciones, 1961 (am. 1985)); asociación o sociedad civil (Código de Comercio, arts. 158+).

Main charitable entity types: Asociación civil y fundación (Código Civil, arts. 109-119, 200-211); instituto de promoción de desarrollo local — registro en SUNARP / Ministerio de Justicia.

Main charitable entity types: asociație (association), fundație (foundation)
Key local requirements: Association 3+ founders (foreigners allowed), local office, Romanian-language statute; foundation 1 founder, endowment per charter, notary deed.
Est. cost & time: ~500 RON state fee + notary ~1,000-2,000 RON; ~1-3 months (statutory 30 days)

Main charitable entity types: Non-profit legal entities (NPL) under the Non-Profit Legal Entities Act; associations; foundations; registered at the Agency for Registration. A 1-founder NPL is the simplest route.
Key local requirements: Nonprofit legal entity (NPL) needs only 1 founder (foreigners allowed) + local office; association needs 5+ founders; Bulgarian-language documents.

Charitable deduction regime: Donations to public-benefit organizations deductible, capped at 10% of annual income.

Tax-exempt status & benefits: PBO status needs separate Central Register entry (Ministry of Justice) - PBOs exempt from CIT when income serves public benefit. Donor deductions: individual 5% of income, corporate 10% of profit.

Tax-exempt status & benefits: General public-benefit status: separate application to the Directorate for Associations (Law 4873/2021); recognized bodies exempt from tax on contributions. Donor cut: 20% of gifts over EUR 100, cap 10% of income.

Main charitable entity types: charitable trust (unregistered), registered body (association), community chest
Key local requirements: A charitable trust needs only a settlor + trustee and no registration; registered body needs 3+ members (foreigners allowed) + local address; English fully accepted.

Main charitable entity types: association (Voluntary Organisations Act (Ch. 492, 2007)), foundation, charitable trust
Key local requirements: Association 3+ founders (foreigners allowed), local registered address; foundation 1 founder, endowment per charter, notary deed; English fully accepted.

Main charitable entity types: Companies limited by guarantee (most charities); incorporated associations; registered with the CRO and then with the Charities Regulatory Authority (CRA).

Main charitable entity types: Registered charity (Charity Commission England & Wales), company limited by guarantee, charitable trust
Key local requirements: Charity must be established and managed in the UK: UK address, UK-based board control, and in practice at least one UK-resident trustee; no citizenship requirement

Main charitable entity types: Associations (felag, 2+ members); foundations (stifting, Act 33/1999); both registered with the Registrator (RSK) under the Directorate of Internal Revenue.

Main charitable entity types: Member associations (lag, unregulated — 2020-21 draft never enacted; simple Brønnøysund registration); foundations; both registered with the Brønnøysund Register. No minimum capital; a simple notification regime.

Main charitable entity types: Associations (yhdistys, 5+ members); foundations (säätiö); registered with PRH (Patent and Registration Office). Charitable status via the Tax Administration.

Main charitable entity types: Economic associations (ekonomiska föreningar); ideal associations; foundations; registered with Bolagsverket (Swedish Companies Registration Office).

Main charitable entity types: Voluntary associations (frivillige foreninger); foundations; associations registered with the CVR register. The Foundations Act (LB 938/2012) applies to foundations.

Tax-exempt status & benefits: Non-commercial association income exempt automatically on CVR registration. Donor deduction: up to DKK 20,000/yr (2026) for gifts to tax-approved orgs under Tax Act s.8A. Time unpublished.
Bank account (remote feasibility): Danish substance — local clients, office or employees — is effectively required; banks demand MitID and strict AML/KYC on foreign owners, so all-non-resident files are often refused; fintech accounts are easier.

Main charitable entity types: Non-profit association (MTÜ), nonprofit foundation (sihtasutus)

Est. cost & time: State fee EUR 30 (MTÜ) / EUR 80 + notary ~40-50 (sihtasutus); 1-3 business days (MTÜ); 5 business days (sihtasutus)

Tax-exempt status & benefits: Registration automatic; separate EMTA list application required (Income Tax Act s.11) - listed orgs: donation income not taxable. Donors: individuals up to EUR 1,200; corporate 3% social tax base or 10% prior profit.
Bank account (remote feasibility): An Estonian bank account is not legally required — EEA EMIs (Wise, LHV online) serve non-resident companies — but Estonian banks approve such files mostly with real local operation or a local board member.

Main charitable entity types: Non-governmental organisations (NVO); associations; foundations; registered in the Enterprise Register under the Law on Associations and Foundations (2014, in force 2015) via the e-portal.

Bank account (remote feasibility): Since the 2018 reforms, business accounts for non-resident owners are hard to approve (2-4 weeks, elevated refusals); banks require proof of a Latvia connection and usually a visit; EU/EEA applicants can apply remotely.

Main charitable entity types: Nonprofit organization (NVO), public benefit institution (viešoji įstaiga), foundation
Key local requirements: Lithuanian address, Lithuanian-language name and documents; NVO needs a board and min. 1–2 founders; registration via e-signature or notary with the Register of Legal Entities

Main charitable entity types: Fundación (private foundation), Asociación (unincorporated association), plus limited charitable societies (SL/SA with statutory purpose)
Key local requirements: Spanish registered office (domicilio social), Spanish-resident legal representative (representante legal), notarial deed of incorporation, and a minimum endowment of ~€30,000 for a fundación
Est. cost & time: €1,500–€3,500 total (notary, registry, legal fees); ~1–3 months including regional foundation registry

Foreign donor / donation restrictions: none notable - no donor registration or licensing; EU free movement of capital applies.

Tax-exempt status & benefits: Foundations with charitable purposes automatically enter Law 49/2002's special regime: profits exempt, donors get a 40% IRPF deduction on the first €15,000 (30% above). No separate AEAT application required.
Bank account (remote feasibility): A cuenta no residente requires a NIE first and an in-person branch visit for KYC and signature. Fully remote opening is not offered by major Spanish banks (BBVA, Santander) for a foreign foundation.

Main charitable entity types: Fundação (private foundation, public-interest institution), Associação (association), and Instituto (institute)
Key local requirements: Portuguese registered office and a locally-based responsible party/director; the foundation deed (estatutos) must be notarised; no statutory minimum endowment, but the granting authority can require a material contribution sufficient for the object to be deemed of public interest
Est. cost & time: €1,000–€2,500 (notary, legal, fees); ~1–2 months for notarisation and public-interest status
Notes: The most straightforward of the four for a foreign founder: no citizenship/residency requirement for the founder, and no fixed minimum capital. Registration fee (USD): none (nominal registration; ~$1,100-2,800 total incl. notary and legal)

Main charitable entity types: Association (Dahir 1-58-376 of 1958, am. 2002; declaration at prefecture); Cooperatives (Law 19-00); foreign associations need Interior Ministry permit

Main charitable entity types: Local CSO and foreign CSO/NGO (CSO Proclamation No. 1113/2019; single-law registration with Civil Society Registry Commission)

Bank account (remote feasibility): In-person application at a bank: passport, local address proof (utility bill/kebele letter) and photos; diaspora accounts serve only Ethiopians abroad; no remote opening.

Main charitable entity types: No independent NGO law; state-controlled associations only; donor funds must pass through government ministries

Main charitable entity types: Association (French Law of 1901 (associations) as amended; declaration at Ministry of Interior); no separate NGO vehicle
Key local requirements: Local registered office, Djiboutian-national chair/meaningful involvement, interior-ministry registration; French/Arabic documents.
Est. cost & time: Fees unpublished; agent costs ~US$100-300; 1-3 months; foreign founders generally need a Djiboutian local representative

Main charitable entity types: NGO (NGO Act 2019, FMOO registration); national and international NGOs; domestic associations under regional law
Key local requirements: Somali founders for a domestic entity; foreign NGOs register through embassy channel; local presence and security plan required.

Main charitable entity types: NGO/welfare organization (Presidential Decree No. 82/11 of 2010; 5+ founders, nationals or foreigners); association

Main charitable entity types: NGO (NGO Act 2016; RRC registration); domestic associations; national and international NGO categories

Main charitable entity types: NPO (Registration of Associations Act 1978, Registry of Associations); Foundation (Foundations Act 2016); Company Limited by Guarantee (Companies Act 2001)
Key local requirements: Mauritian registered office (local agent provides it); foreign founders/directors permitted; NPOs have a local-presence element.

Main charitable entity types: Public charitable trust (state trust deeds), registered society, Section 8 company (Companies Act 2013)

Main charitable entity types: Public charitable trust (trust deed), Section 42 non-profit company (Companies Act 2017), registered society

Main charitable entity types: Public charitable trust (Trusts Ordinance (Cap. 72), Commissioner of Charities); Company Limited by Guarantee (Companies Act 2007); association (Companies Act s.34)

Key local requirements: Russian-language filings, foreign-agent law risks for foreign-linked orgs, sanctions on AU side
Est. cost & time: n/a for foreign founders - MoJ registration requires a Russian legal base and state policy; foreign-founded NGOs are effectively barred (foreign-agent law expanded 1 Dec 2022).
Notes: No GfN. Sanctions + foreign-agent regime make this unsuitable for an Australian founder. | Confirm prior: public organization/foundation via Ministry of Justice, hard difficulty; fee is modest (~$45) but foreign-agent regime makes it unsuitable.
Main bottleneck (remote foreign founder): Needs a Russian legal address and locally-present leadership; remote founders rely on a local agent (notarized documents).
Time to register: 4-8 weeks (MoJ decision within 30 days plus document notarization/translation)
Charitable deduction regime: Charitable donations deductible from personal income tax up to 25% of taxable income (Tax Code Art. 219).
Foreign donor / donation restrictions: Foreign agent label if >10% foreign funding/support; 'undesirable organization' designation possible; AU sanctions risk.
Annual compliance & reporting: NCOs file an annual activity report plus financial statements to the tax authority (within 3 months of fiscal year end); 'foreign agent' NCOs file quarterly reports to Minjust; fines for non-compliance.
Tax-exempt status & benefits: NCO registered with Ministry of Justice (Federal Law 7-FZ (1996)); not automatically tax-exempt - apply to tax office for exemption from profit/property tax (non-profit, commercial income under 30%); no donor deduction; 30-90 days.
Bank account (remote feasibility): Foreigners with legal stay can open accounts in person (Law 395-1), but a remote founder has no such grounds, and sanctions isolate Russian banks from SWIFT - access is effectively blocked for foreigners abroad.
